title: Castle in the Sky
subtitle: Many have heard its name, yet few know its truth.

items.text: Yard, School of Mei

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Come, Mayfly. You ought to familiarize yourself with our school before you begin.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Yes, Master.
Mayfly peeks out from behind the door, watching the others in the front courtyard.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: It's still early in the morning, but everyone's already up and busy.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: It is. Soon, you will be practicing alongside them.
The many Yao she has come to know nod to her in greeting.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: The students live in the side house here, as will you. I believe you've met some of them already.

items.speaker: Quick Mouse
items.text: *squeak*

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I see, ah! There's a mouse climbing up on that bamboo by the wall.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Heh. Don't be alarmed by Brother Mouse. He has taken to staying in his true form most of the day.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: F-Forgive me, Brother.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: I'm sure he does not mind. The School of Mei is one of the few refuges for Yao in this region. Our students are free to live in whatever form they wish. You may even choose to live as a reed, if that is what you desire.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Live in my true form. But I ...

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: One must learn to find fulfillment in their true nature; only then may one discern their path to the Way. It will make sense in time.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Hmm.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Come. Let us speak further in the front courtyard.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Master, where is that music coming from? I keep hearing it, but I don't see anyone playing.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: You won't have need of that haste much longer, Sister Mayfly.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: This is the front courtyard, where students may gather to train or rest as they like.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: But no one's here.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: This way.
The gardens of this land excel at artful concealment. Past the moon gate, after a few winding paths, a hidden world opens up to her.
Black eaves press down upon white rooms that enclose a square. The ground is paved with gravel, into which white marble tiles are set, forming a Bagua array.
Students in white stand atop it, playing solemn Daoist music together.

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: There she is, the new student!

items.speaker: Hedgehog
items.text: Sister Mayfly, are you feeling better?
Paper Heron waits here too. The students occasionally steal small glances at her.
She looks around, nodding to the students as she meets their eyes and greeting Mayfly in particular.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Hello, everyone, what are you all doing here?

items.speaker: All Yao
items.text: Master Rén is here too!

items.speaker: All Yao
items.text: Greetings, Master! We humbly request your guidance this day!

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: It's good to see you all. Please, be seated.
The crowd spreads out and sits in a ring around Master Rén. A female Yao pulls Mayfly in to sit beside her.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Revision always offers new insight. And with a new student among us today, let us begin by reviewing the stages of the Method of Longevity.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: To master this art, one must attain three stages: the regulation of Qi, concentration and visualization, and the cultivation of the body.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: In the first stage, we focus on the rhythm of the breath. Each of you must find the pace which best suits your constitution and nature.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Once you reach a state of meditation, we will work to concentrate the mind on an object, opening ourselves to the stimuli of the divine, as for the cultivation of the body.
Hearing this, Paper Heron interrupts Master Rén.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: That wouldn't be for the best.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Whatever do you mean, Master?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Your students are getting ahead of themselves. Teach them the basics first, eh? A pavilion is not built from the roof down.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: If I am to cover every foundational detail, I would have to start from before the White Horse School was even founded.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Unfortunately, I never walked its halls. All that I know, I learned from you. Would you do us the honor, Grandmaster?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: The students would be most grateful to hear it from your lips.
Paper Heron looks around. The students wait eagerly for her words. The School of Mei seems to be thriving on the high morale of its students, and her heart is warmed by it.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: It has been quite some time since I last spoke of my old school, but I'd be happy to.
She lifts her heels and leaps gracefully into the ring before launching into her story.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: The very first attempts at achieving longevity can be traced back to ancient times, but it's enough to start with the founding of the White Horse School, eh?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: It first took shape in the late Tang Dynasty, as our founding master traveled the land collecting many rare and lost scriptures in hopes of preserving the Daoist arts for future generations.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: From those arts, he developed a method to balance Yin and Yang, and through it, discovered the secret to a long life.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: He named it The Practice of Inner Alchemy, and it later became the foundation of the White Horse School.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Now, to perform it properly, you must work through these stages in order. Listen closely.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: The scripture says, "When one's mind is tranquil and free of distracting thoughts, all things between heaven and earth will become one with it." So, the first step is to set aside worldly concerns and seek stillness from within, for only then can one perceive the presence of the Way.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Step two is about finding your Qi. "Life is born of the accumulation of Qi. When Qi gathers, we live; when it disperses, we perish."

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Without Qi, we can neither strengthen our bodies nor nourish our spirits, and so we cannot prolong our lives. We must spend years learning its workings, until it becomes as familiar to us as our own hands.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: The third step is to use your understanding of Qi to work its flow, guiding it until it moves in harmony with the Way.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: This step is the most crucial—when your body attunes itself to your Qi and allows you to retain it. This may take some time, but it must not be rushed.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: "Without the Qi within, the body stands hollow. And if hollow, how may life endure in it?"

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: This takes real devotion. You must practice daily until your body is ready to harmonize with the flow of Qi.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: "To retain Qi is to attain the Way; one who has attained the Way may long endure," so the scripture says.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But the path is long and perilous. Stray from it, and both body and spirit may be annihilated.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: At best, it is a process of decades; at worst, well, I've seen some wait hundreds of years.

items.speaker: Hedgehog
items.text: But, Grandmaster ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Yes? Speak your mind.

items.speaker: Hedgehog
items.text: Do you really mean it will take a few decades for us to master this method?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: To walk the path of longevity is no small feat. But the calmer your mind, the clearer your vision, and the quicker you will progress.

items.speaker: Hedgehog
items.text: But how can I devote myself to a method that takes decades to master when I only have a few years to live? And if what you say is true, wouldn't only the long-lived be able to achieve longevity?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah!
She pauses, composing her thoughts for a long while, then walks over to the Gen trigram.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Not entirely. The scripture says, "In the pursuit of worldly knowledge, one gains daily. In the pursuit of the Way, one loses daily. Less and less is done, until nothing is done. When nothing is done, nothing is left undone."

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Don't get so hung up on the path ahead. Nothing stays fixed forever. Live in the moment, and new opportunities will arise.

items.speaker: Hedgehog
items.text: So we'll just do nothing at all?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Not exactly. It isn't nothing but rather "non-action." We let go of all deliberate effort, attending to your purposes, doing only that which is yours to do.
Hearing her words, the Yao look at each other. One of them cannot hold back their frustration and rushes up in front of her.

items.speaker: Badger
items.text: That's absurd!

items.speaker: Badger
items.text: If that's how it is, what are we to do? Sit around and wait for death to come? Our lives are much shorter than yours, you know!

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Now, now, Brother Badger. The grandmaster didn't mean ...
Undeterred by the gentle redirection, the Yao continues his questions anyway.

items.speaker: Badger
items.text: "That which is yours to do." What's that supposed to mean? Is this "what's mine to do"?

items.speaker: Hedgehog
items.text: Grandmaster, none of us would be here if we had been content with the time we were given.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah ...
Paper Heron is speechless. She sees now the crux of the issue; they have been led astray from the very beginning.
The doubting voices grow louder. The Yao become agitated. Paper Heron stands silent above them, lost. Mayfly struggles in her seat, not knowing who to agree with.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Alright, everyone.
A clear, loud call rings out like a stone dropped in water. The Yao immediately fall silent.

items.speaker: Badger
items.text: Master.
Master Rén walks into the ring and stands beside her teacher.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Each of us approaches the Way differently, for we are all guided by our own nature. The grandmaster speaks only from her own experience.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: If her words help you, hold them. If they muddle you, do not be troubled. You may understand them in the time to come.

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Yes, Master.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: It's been a long day, and the grandmaster has traveled far. Please, leave her to rest.
Paper Heron looks at her former student and then at the calmed Yao. With a stiff nod, she resigns herself to a stone stool outside the ring.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Heron, are you alright?
She walks over and sits by Paper Heron, whose serene facade now seems ever so subtly broken.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I'm fine. Should've chosen my words with more care, though.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Well ...
For a moment, the cicada chirps and bird calls sound unusually sharp.
Paper Heron looks down, hiding her face.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I thought they'd be interested. Back in my time ...
The words are a faint whisper, so light she barely hears them.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What do you mean?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Nothing. Just forget what I've said and follow your master's teachings.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Perhaps she's found a better way.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: The third step the grandmaster spoke of is what we call the "cultivation of the body." Through practice, your body will work with your Qi until they are one.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Mastering this may take decades, even hundreds of years, but here in the School of Mei, we needn't dwell on that step. Instead, we focus on the regulation of Qi, and concentration and visualization.
She looks over to Master Rén as she continues her lesson and resolves herself to what must be done.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: "We needn't dwell on that step"?
